title: Late PET/CT acquisition for improved tissue characterization and assessment of treatment response: prospective data collection in clinically indicated examinations in oncology.
summary:
For the determination of tumor spread and therapy planning, imaging by means of PET/CT (positron emission tomography, combined with computed tomography) is the current standard of diagnostics. Nevertheless, this method is to be improved continuously, since a tumor and its possibly existing metastases can behave very differently. Tracer imaging could be used to estimate the response to therapy. Here, it is particularly important to delineate metastases with different biological characteristics.

With conventional PET/CT devices, only a short period of time after tracer administration could be examined, since the radioactive substances used here decay very quickly. The newly developed Biograph Vision Quadra® PET/CT scanner (Siemens) also enables significantly later measurement times due to its higher sensitivity. This makes it possible for the first time to observe metabolic processes that occur slowly. This can be important for oncological imagiing, as it is assumed that metastases change independently and respond differently to therapies. It is also often problematic to confidently distinguish inflammatory tissue, scar tissue, and tumor tissue. However, since it is assumed that tumor tissue, scar tissue and inflammatory tissue respectively metabolize the radioactive substance at different rates, an (additional) late PET measurement may contribute to a better differentiation. 

The aim of the study is to better identify the different biological behavior of these different tissue types by means of a second or third PET examination within a time interval of two to eleven hours.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Justifying clinical indication for PET/CT examination,
- Patients with predominantly one of the following oncological diseases: Lymphoma (Hodgkin's, non-Hodgkin's), prostate cancer, neuroendocrine tumors, patients treated with radiation oncology (esophageal cancer, head and neck tumors, lung cancer, rectal cancer, anal cancer), cholangiocellular carcinoma, malignant melanoma, CUP, thyroid carcinoma
- Patients able to grasp the nature and extent of pseudonymized prospective data collection,
- Patients who can tolerate a waiting time of 2-11 hours between regular and late PET/CT measurements with a maximum examination time of 30-60 minutes in the PET/CT scanner,
- Age ≥18 years,
- Written informed consent from the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnant and breastfeeding women,
- Patients with claustrophobia,
- Patients with severely reduced general condition and/or problems/pain when lying on their backs, so that waiting time and further lying time may not be tolerated,
- Exclusion criteria according to Radiation Protection Ordinance, 
- Limited capacity of the patient to give consent.
